failures: deploy/entrypoint.sh has no line-ending protection: the repo has no .gitattributes and the Dockerfile does not normalize it. On a Windows checkout with core.autocrlf=true (this user's config) the script is CRLF, `docker compose build app` still succeeds, but the container cannot start ('exec /app/deploy/entrypoint.sh: no such file or directory', rc 255). Reproduce: git clone the commit, check `file deploy/entrypoint.sh`, build, `docker run -e SPROUT_SECRET_KEY=x <image>`. The smoke test passes only because the worktree file happens to be LF. Fix: add .gitattributes with `*.sh text eol=lf` (and/or sed -i 's/\r$//' in the Dockerfile) and a test that the entrypoint has no CR.
notes: Only the CRLF problem is a failure. Minor: base image not pinned by digest, so a clean rebuild may change OS packages; a whitespace-only or very short SPROUT_SECRET_KEY is accepted; /data is only writable by sprout for named volumes (bind mounts or Cloud Run volumes may be root-owned, and docs do not mention the uid 10001 requirement); /models/fastembed is root-owned, so the cache must be pre-filled as docs say. Setting SPROUT_ENV=testing in production is still an explicit way to enable the fake; the default is production and docs say not to. Worker sizing is honestly deferred to T7.4. I removed my image t73v-img; images t73-app and sprout-serve-test belong to the implementer's runs and were left. My temp context and clone are in orchestration/evidence/tmp-T7.3/ (git-ignored).
